content: Melvin-Koushki contrasts the doctrine of philosophia perennis, which sees the wisdom tradition as static and, by placing the golden age at the dawn of time, must posit the ineluctable decline of history and is profoundly conservative, with the prisca-theologia paradox of progress through recovery, which he says was never adequately resolved but was a source of creative dynamism. He then asks what of complexity, arguing that entropy is counterbalanced by growth in complexity.
